sentences.zh: 潘宗顏，字士瓚，保安衛人。

translations.literal: Pan Zongyan, courtesy name Shizan, was a native of the Bao'an Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Zongyan, styled Shizan, came from the Bao'an Guard.

sentences.zh: 善詩賦，曉天文、兵法。

translations.literal: He was skilled at poetry and rhapsodies, and understood astronomy and military science.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at poetry and composition and understood astronomy and the art of war.

sentences.zh: 舉萬曆四十一年進士，歷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination and served successively as a bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 41 he passed the jinshi examination and rose to bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 數上書當路言遼事，當路不能用。

translations.literal: He repeatedly submitted memorials to those in power on Liaodong affairs, but those in power could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized those in power about Liaodong, but they would not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 以宗顏知兵，命督餉遼東。

translations.literal: Because Zongyan was known to understand warfare, he was ordered to supervise grain supplies in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Since Zongyan was known to understand military affairs, he was ordered to supervise grain supplies in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 旋擢開原兵備僉事。

translations.literal: He was soon promoted to assistant commissioner for military preparations at Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to assistant commissioner for military preparations at Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，馬林將出師，宗顏上書經略楊鎬曰：「林庸懦，不堪當一面，乞易他將，以林為後繼，不然必敗。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year, when Ma Lin was about to take the field, Zongyan memorialized the supreme commander Yang Hao: "Lin is mediocre and cowardly, unfit to hold one wing of the army. I beg that another general be substituted for him and Lin be kept in reserve; otherwise defeat is certain.
translations.idiomatic: In year 46, as Ma Lin was about to take the field, Zongyan wrote to the supreme commander Yang Hao: "Lin is mediocre and timid, unfit to hold one wing. I beg you replace him with another general and keep Lin in reserve—otherwise you are certain to be defeated.

sentences.zh: 」鎬不從。

translations.literal: " Hao would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " Hao would not listen.

sentences.zh: 宗顏監林軍，出三岔口，營稗子峪，夜聞杜松敗，林軍遂嘩。

translations.literal: Zongyan supervised Lin's army, marched out through Sanchakou, and encamped at Beizi Valley; at night they heard that Du Song had been defeated, and Lin's troops immediately broke into clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan supervised Lin's army, marched out through Sanchakou, and encamped at Beizi Valley. That night they heard Du Song had been defeated, and Lin's troops fell into uproar.

sentences.zh: 及旦，大清兵大至。

translations.literal: At dawn the Great Qing army arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the Qing army arrived in overwhelming strength.

sentences.zh: 林恐甚，一戰而敗，策馬先奔。

translations.literal: Lin was greatly afraid; after one battle he was defeated and spurred his horse to flee first.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was terrified; after a single engagement he was routed and spurred his horse to flee ahead of all others.

sentences.zh: 守顏殿後，奮呼沖擊，膽氣彌厲。

translations.literal: Zongyan covered the rear, shouting as he charged forward, his courage growing ever fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Zongyan covered the rear, shouting as he charged; his courage only grew fiercer.

sentences.zh: 自辰至午，力不支，與遊擊竇永澄、守備江萬春、贊理通判董爾礪等皆死焉。

translations.literal: From the hour chen until the hour wu his strength gave out; he died together with the battalion commander Dou Yongcheng, garrison commander Jiang Wanchun, supervising secretary Tongpan Dong Erli, and others.
translations.idiomatic: From the hour chen until wu his strength gave out, and he died together with the battalion commander Dou Yongcheng, garrison commander Jiang Wanchun, supervising secretary Dong Erli, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜祭葬，贈光祿卿，再贈大理卿，蔭錦衣世百戶，謚節湣，立祠奉祀。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was granted sacrificial rites and burial, posthumously ennobled as Vice Minister of the Imperial Household, then posthumously ennobled again as Minister of Justice, his family granted hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred households, given the posthumous title Jiemin, and a shrine established for worship.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was granted state sacrifices and burial, posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Household and then Minister of Justice, his heirs granted hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred households, given the posthumous title Jiemin, and a shrine was established for his worship.

sentences.zh: 永澄等亦賜恤如制。

translations.literal: Yongcheng and the others were also granted consolation according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng and the others received condolence grants according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 張銓，字宇衡，沁水人。

translations.literal: Zhang Quan, courtesy name Yuheng, was a native of Qinshui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Quan, styled Yuheng, came from Qinshui.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十二年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 32.

sentences.zh: 授保定推官，擢御史，巡視陜西茶馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Baoding, then promoted to censor and toured Shaanxi inspecting the tea-horse trade.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of Baoding, then promoted to censor and toured Shaanxi to oversee the tea-horse trade.

sentences.zh: 以憂歸，起按江西。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning, then was recalled to serve as touring inspector of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He went home for mourning, then was recalled to serve as touring inspector of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時遼東總兵官張承蔭敗歿，而經略楊鎬方議四道出師。

translations.literal: At the time the Liaodong commander-in-chief Zhang Chengyin had been defeated and killed, while the supreme commander Yang Hao was deliberating a four-route advance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Liaodong commander-in-chief Zhang Chengyin had been defeated and killed, while the supreme commander Yang Hao was planning a four-route advance.

sentences.zh: 銓馳奏言：「敵山川險易，我未能悉知，懸軍深入，保無抄絕？

translations.literal: Quan urgently memorialized: "The enemy's mountains and rivers, steep and easy ground—we have not fully understood them; to suspend the army deep in enemy territory—can we be sure of no interception and cut-off?
translations.idiomatic: Quan urgently memorialized: "We do not fully know the enemy's terrain, steep or easy. To drive deep into hostile country—can we be sure of no ambush or cut-off?

sentences.zh: 且突騎野戰，敵所長，我所短。

translations.literal: Moreover, in sudden-cavalry field battles the enemy excels and we are deficient.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden cavalry charges in open battle are what the enemy does best and we do worst.

sentences.zh: 以短擊長，以勞赴逸，以客當主，非計也。

translations.literal: To strike the long with the short, to meet ease with exhaustion, to meet the host as the guest—this is not a plan.
translations.idiomatic: To pit our weakness against their strength, our exhaustion against their rest, and the guest against the host—this is no strategy at all.

sentences.zh: 昔臚朐河之戰，五將不還，奈何輕出塞。

translations.literal: In the battle of Lujuqie River of old five generals did not return; why lightly go beyond the passes?
translations.idiomatic: At the battle of Lujuqie River five generals never returned—why venture lightly beyond the frontier?

sentences.zh: 為今計，不必徵兵四方，但當就近調募，屯集要害以固吾圉，厚撫北關以樹其敵，多行間諜以攜其黨，然後伺隙而動。

translations.literal: As the present plan, there is no need to levy troops from the four quarters; one need only recruit nearby, mass at critical points to secure our defenses, treat the northern passes generously to set up enemies against them, send many spies to disrupt their faction, and then await an opening to act.
translations.idiomatic: The present plan need not levy troops from every quarter; recruit nearby, mass at critical points to hold our defenses, treat the northern passes generously to set enemies against them, send many spies to sow discord in their ranks, and then wait for an opening.

sentences.zh: 若加賦選丁，騷擾天下，恐識者之憂不在遼東。

translations.literal: If additional levies and conscription disturb the empire, those with discernment will fear their worry lies not in Liaodong alone.
translations.idiomatic: If extra taxes and conscription throw the empire into turmoil, men of discernment will fear the danger lies not in Liaodong alone.

sentences.zh: 」因請發帑金，補大僚，宥直言，開儲講，先為自治之本。

translations.literal: " He therefore requested disbursing treasury silver, filling high offices, pardoning outspoken criticism, opening the crown prince's schooling, and establishing self-rule as the foundation first.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore asked that treasury funds be released, high offices filled, outspoken critics pardoned, and the crown prince's schooling opened—establishing self-government as the foundation first.

sentences.zh: 又言：「李如柏、杜松、劉綎以宿將並起，宜責鎬約束，以一事權。

translations.literal: He also said: "Li Rubai, Du Song, and Liu Ting—all veteran generals rising together—Hao should be charged to restrain them and unify command in one hand.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Li Rubai, Du Song, and Liu Ting are all veteran generals rising together. Hao should be charged to restrain them and unify command in one hand.

sentences.zh: 唐九節度相州之潰，可為明鑒。

translations.literal: The Tang collapse of the nine frontier commissioners at Xiangzhou can serve as a clear mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang disaster when nine frontier commissioners acted at cross purposes at Xiangzhou should be a clear warning.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「廷議將恤承蔭，夫承蔭不知敵誘，輕進取敗，是謂無謀。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The court deliberates condoling Chengyin. Chengyin did not know the enemy's trickery, advanced lightly and was defeated—this is called having no strategy.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "The court deliberates condoling Chengyin. Chengyin did not recognize the enemy's ruse, advanced rashly, and was defeated—that is having no strategy.

sentences.zh: 猝與敵遇，行列錯亂，是謂無法。

translations.literal: Encountering the enemy suddenly, ranks in disorder—this is called having no discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the enemy suddenly with ranks in disorder—that is having no discipline.

sentences.zh: 率萬餘之眾，不能死戰，是謂無勇。

translations.literal: Leading a host of more than ten thousand yet unable to die fighting—this is called having no courage.
translations.idiomatic: Leading more than ten thousand men yet unable to fight to the death—that is having no courage.

sentences.zh: 臣以為不宜恤。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that he should not be condoled.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant holds that he should not be condoled.

sentences.zh: 」又論鎬非大帥才，而力薦熊廷弼。

translations.literal: " He also argued that Hao was not talent for a supreme commander, and strongly recommended Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: " He also argued that Hao lacked the talent of a supreme commander and strongly recommended Xiong Tingbi.

sentences.zh: 四十八年夏復上疏言：「自軍興以來，所司創議加賦，畝增銀三厘，未幾至七厘，又未幾至九厘。

translations.literal: In summer of the forty-eighth year he again memorialized: "Since the opening of hostilities the responsible offices have devised additional levies: three cash per mu of land, before long seven cash, before long nine cash.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of year 48 he memorialized again: "Since the war began the responsible offices have devised extra levies—three cash per mu, then before long seven, then before long nine.

sentences.zh: 辟之一身，遼東，肩背也，天下，腹心也。

translations.literal: It may be compared to a single body: Liaodong is the shoulders and back; the empire is the heart and belly.
translations.idiomatic: Compare it to a single body: Liaodong is the shoulders and back; the empire is the heart and belly.

sentences.zh: 肩背有患，猶藉腹心之血脈滋灌。

translations.literal: When the shoulders and back are afflicted, one may still rely on the blood and vessels of the heart and belly to nourish and irrigate.
translations.idiomatic: When the shoulders and back are afflicted, one may still draw on the blood and vessels of the heart and belly to nourish them.

sentences.zh: 若腹心先潰，危亡可立待。

translations.literal: If the heart and belly collapse first, peril and destruction can be awaited immediately.
translations.idiomatic: If the heart and belly collapse first, ruin can be awaited at once.

sentences.zh: 竭天下以救遼，遼未必安，而天下已危。

translations.literal: Exhausting the empire to save Liaodong—Liaodong may not be secure, yet the empire is already endangered.
translations.idiomatic: Exhaust the empire to save Liaodong and Liaodong may not be saved, yet the empire is already in peril.

sentences.zh: 今宜聯人心以固根本，豈可朘削無已，驅之使亂。

translations.literal: Now one should unite human hearts to consolidate the root foundation; how can one pare away without end and drive the people to disorder?
translations.idiomatic: Now is the time to unite hearts and secure the foundation. How can we pare away without end and drive the people to rebellion?

sentences.zh: 且陛下內廷積金如山，以有用之物，置無用之地，與瓦礫糞土何異。

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty's inner court has gold piled like mountains—placing useful things in a useless place, what difference from rubble and dung?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Your Majesty's inner court has gold piled like mountains—placing what is useful in a useless place is no different from rubble and dung.

sentences.zh: 乃發帑之請，叫閽不應，加派之議，朝奏夕可。

translations.literal: Yet requests to open the treasury go unanswered at the gate, while proposals for additional levies are approved the evening of the morning they are memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pleas to open the treasury go unanswered at the gate, while proposals for extra levies are approved the same evening they are submitted.

sentences.zh: 臣殊不得其解。

translations.literal: Your servant finds it utterly inexplicable.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant finds this utterly beyond understanding.

sentences.zh: 」銓疏皆關軍國安危，而帝與當軸卒不省。

translations.literal: Quan's memorials all bore on the security of army and state, yet the emperor and those at the helm ultimately took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's memorials all bore on the security of army and state, yet the emperor and those at the helm took no notice.

sentences.zh: 綎、松敗，時謂銓有先見云。

translations.literal: When Ting and Song were defeated, the age said Quan had foresight.
translations.idiomatic: When Ting and Song were defeated, the age said Quan had foreseen it.

sentences.zh: 熹宗即位，出按遼東，經略袁應泰下納降令，銓力爭，不聽，曰：「禍始此矣。

translations.literal: When the Xizong Emperor acceded, Quan went out to inspect Liaodong; the frontier commander Yuan Yingtai issued an order accepting surrenders. Quan argued strenuously but was not heeded, saying: "Disaster begins here.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xizong acceded, Quan went out to inspect Liaodong. The frontier commander Yuan Yingtai issued an order accepting surrenders. Quan argued strenuously but was not heeded, saying, "Disaster begins here.

sentences.zh: 」天啟元年三月，瀋陽破，銓請令遼東巡撫薛國用帥河西兵駐海州，薊遼總督文球帥山海兵駐廣寧，以壯聲援。

translations.literal: " In the third month of Tianqi 1, Shenyang fell; Quan requested that the Liaodong grand coordinator Xue Guoyong lead Hexi troops to garrison Haizhou, and that the Jizhou-Liaodong supreme commander Wen Qiu lead Shanhai troops to garrison Guangning, to strengthen vocal support.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third month of Tianqi 1, Shenyang fell. Quan asked that Liaodong grand coordinator Xue Guoyong lead Hexi troops to garrison Haizhou and Jizhou-Liaodong supreme commander Wen Qiu lead Shanhai troops to garrison Guangning, to strengthen the show of support.

sentences.zh: 疏甫上，遼陽被圍，軍大潰。

translations.literal: The memorial had just gone up when Liaoyang was besieged and the army collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial had scarcely been submitted when Liaoyang was besieged and the army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 銓與應泰分城守，應泰令銓退保河西，以圖再舉，不從。

translations.literal: Quan and Yingtai divided the city in defense; Yingtai ordered Quan to withdraw and hold the west of the river to plan another effort, but he would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and Yingtai divided the defense of the city. Yingtai ordered Quan to withdraw west of the river and plan another effort, but Quan refused.

sentences.zh: 守三日，城破，被執不屈，欲殺之，引頸待刃，乃送歸署。

translations.literal: After defending three days the city fell; seized, he would not submit. They wished to kill him; he stretched his neck awaiting the blade, and they sent him back to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After three days the city fell. Captured, he would not yield. When they meant to kill him, he stretched his neck to the blade, and they sent him back to headquarters instead.

sentences.zh: 銓衣冠向闕拜，又遙拜父母，遂自經。

translations.literal: Quan in full dress bowed toward the palace, then bowed from afar to his parents, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Quan dressed in his official robes, bowed toward the palace, then bowed toward his parents from afar, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈大理卿，再贈兵部尚書，謚忠烈。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Justice, then posthumously ennobled again as Minister of War, and given the posthumous title Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Minister of Justice and then Minister of War, with the posthumous title Zhonglie.

sentences.zh: 官其子道浚錦衣指揮僉事。

translations.literal: His son Daojun was appointed battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Daojun was appointed battalion commander in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 銓父五典，歷官南京大理卿，時侍養家居。

translations.literal: Quan's father Wudian had served as Minister of Justice at Nanjing and was at home caring for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Quan's father Wudian had served as Minister of Justice at Nanjing and was at home caring for his parents.

sentences.zh: 詔以銓所贈官加之，及卒，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: An edict added to him the offices posthumously granted Quan; when he died he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict added to him the offices posthumously granted Quan. When he died, he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，五典度海內將亂，築所居竇莊為堡，堅甚。

translations.literal: Earlier Wudian judged that the empire would fall into disorder and built his residence at Dou Village into a fortress, very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wudian foresaw that the empire would fall into disorder and fortified his residence at Dou Village into a stronghold.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年，流賊至，五典已歿，獨銓妻霍氏在，眾請避之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chongzhen bandits arrived; Wudian was already dead, and only Quan's wife Lady Huo remained. The crowd urged her to flee.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 4 bandits arrived. Wudian was already dead, and only Quan's wife Lady Huo remained. The others urged her to flee.

sentences.zh: 曰：「避賊而出，家不保。

translations.literal: She said: "Fleeing the bandits and going out—the household cannot be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: She said, "If we flee the bandits and leave, the household cannot be saved.

sentences.zh: 出而遇賊，身更不保。

translations.literal: Going out and meeting the bandits, one's person is even less preserved.
translations.idiomatic: If we go out and meet the bandits, our lives are even less secure.

sentences.zh: 等死耳，盍死於家。

translations.literal: Death is equal in either case—why not die at home?
translations.idiomatic: Death is the same either way—why not die at home?

sentences.zh: 」乃率僮仆堅守。

translations.literal: " She then led the servants and retainers in a stout defense.
translations.idiomatic: " She then led the servants and retainers in a stout defense.

sentences.zh: 賊環攻四晝夜，不克而去。

translations.literal: The bandits besieged it for four days and nights without taking it and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits besieged it for four days and nights, failed to take it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 副使王肇生名其堡曰「夫人城」。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Wang Zhaosheng named the fortress "Lady's City."
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Wang Zhaosheng named the fortress "Lady's City."

sentences.zh: 鄉人避賊者多賴以免。

translations.literal: Many of the local people who fled the bandits relied on it to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Many locals who fled the bandits owed their survival to it.

sentences.zh: 道浚既官錦衣，以忠臣子見重，屢加都指揮僉事，僉書衛所。

translations.literal: Once Daojun held office in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, as the son of a loyal minister he was highly regarded and repeatedly promoted to vice commander of the guard, with concurrent duties in the guard offices.
translations.idiomatic: Once Daojun held office in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, he was highly regarded as the son of a loyal minister and was repeatedly promoted to vice commander, with concurrent duties in the guard offices.

sentences.zh: 顧與閹黨楊維垣等相善，而受王永光指，攻錢龍錫、成基命等，為公論所不予。

translations.literal: Yet he was on good terms with the eunuch faction's Yang Weiyuan and others, and under Wang Yongguang's direction attacked Qian Longxi, Cheng Jiming, and others, winning no favor from public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was friendly with eunuch-faction men such as Yang Weiyuan and, at Wang Yongguang's direction, attacked Qian Longxi and Cheng Jiming—acts that won no favor in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 尋以納賄事敗，戍雁門。

translations.literal: Soon he was exposed for taking bribes and was banished to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was exposed for taking bribes and was banished to Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 流賊起，山西巡撫宋統殷檄道浚軍前贊畫。

translations.literal: When bandits rose, Shanxi grand coordinator Song Tongyin summoned Daojun to the front as planning aide.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose, Shanxi grand coordinator Song Tongyin summoned Daojun to the front as planning aide.

sentences.zh: 道浚家多壯丁，能禦賊。

translations.literal: Daojun's household had many strong young men able to resist bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun's household had many strong young men who could fight bandits.

sentences.zh: 崇禎五年四月，賊犯沁水，寧武守備猛忠戰死。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Chongzhen bandits invaded Qinshui; Ningwu garrison commander Meng Zhong died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chongzhen 5 bandits invaded Qinshui, and Ningwu garrison commander Meng Zhong died fighting.

sentences.zh: 道浚遣遊擊張瓚馳援，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Daojun sent battalion commander Zhang Zan in haste to relieve them, and the bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun sent battalion commander Zhang Zan in haste to relieve them, and the bandits withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八月，紫金梁、老回回、八金剛等以三萬眾圍竇莊，謀執道浚以脅巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Zijinliang, Old Huihui, Eight Vajras, and others with thirty thousand men besieged Dou Village, planning to seize Daojun to coerce the grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Zijinliang, Old Huihui, Eight Vajras, and others besieged Dou Village with thirty thousand men, planning to seize Daojun to coerce the grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 道浚屢敗賊，賊乃欲因道浚求撫。

translations.literal: Daojun repeatedly defeated the bandits, and the bandits then wished through Daojun to seek pacification.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun repeatedly defeated them, and the bandits then sought pacification through him.

sentences.zh: 紫金梁請見，免胄前曰：「我王自用也，誤從王佳胤至此。

translations.literal: Zijinliang requested an audience, removed his helmet, and came forward saying: "I was used by my king; I erred in following Wang Jiayin here.
translations.idiomatic: Zijinliang requested an audience, removed his helmet, and came forward saying, "I was used by my king. I erred in following Wang Jiayin here.

sentences.zh: 」又一人跽致辭曰：「我宜川廩生韓廷憲，為佳胤所獲，請誓死奉約束。

translations.literal: " Another man knelt and spoke: "I am Yichuan stipend student Han Tingxian, captured by Jiayin. I beg to swear to obey unto death.
translations.idiomatic: " Another man knelt and said, "I am Yichuan stipend student Han Tingxian, captured by Jiayin. I beg to swear to obey you unto death.

sentences.zh: 」道浚勞遣之，而陰使使啗廷憲圖賊。

translations.literal: " Daojun comforted them and sent them off, while secretly sending an envoy to entice Tingxian to plot against the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " Daojun comforted them and sent them off, while secretly sending an envoy to win Tingxian over to plot against the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊至舊縣，守約不動，廷憲日惎紫金梁就款，未決。

translations.literal: The bandits reached Jiuxian and kept the agreement without moving; day by day Tingxian urged Zijinliang to submit, but no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits reached Jiuxian and kept the agreement without moving. Day after day Tingxian urged Zijinliang to submit, but no decision was reached.

sentences.zh: 官軍襲之，賊怒，尤廷憲，遂敗約，南突濟源，陷溫陽。

translations.literal: Government troops raided them; the bandits were enraged and blamed Tingxian above all, broke the agreement, burst south into Jiyuan, and took Wenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops raided them. The bandits were enraged and blamed Tingxian above all, broke the agreement, burst south into Jiyuan, and took Wenyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，廷憲知紫金梁疑己，思殺之以歸，約道浚伏兵沁河以待。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Tingxian knew Zijinliang suspected him and thought to kill him to return to allegiance; he arranged with Daojun to set an ambush on the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Tingxian knew Zijinliang suspected him and planned to kill him and return to allegiance. He arranged with Daojun to set an ambush on the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 道浚遣所部劉偉佐之。

translations.literal: Daojun sent his subordinate Liu Wei to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun sent his subordinate Liu Wei to assist.

sentences.zh: 是夕，賊攻諸生蓋汝璋樓，掘地深丈餘，樓不毀。

translations.literal: That evening the bandits attacked the tower of student Gai Ruzhang, digging more than a zhang into the ground, yet the tower was not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: That evening the bandits attacked student Gai Ruzhang's tower, digging more than a zhang into the ground, yet the tower would not fall.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，誓必拔。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged and swore they must take it.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, they swore they would take it at all costs.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴不得間，廷憲知事且泄，偕偉倉卒奔。

translations.literal: At cockcrow they had no respite; Tingxian knew the affair would soon be exposed and fled in haste with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow they had no respite. Tingxian knew the plot would soon be exposed and fled in haste with Wei.

sentences.zh: 賊追之及河，伏起，殺追者滾山虎等六人，皆賊腹心也。

translations.literal: The bandits pursued them to the river; the ambush rose and killed six pursuers including Gunshanhu—all trusted men of the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits pursued them to the river. The ambush rose and killed six pursuers including Gunshanhu—all trusted men of the bandits.

sentences.zh: 賊臨沁河，索廷憲。

translations.literal: The bandits came to the Qin River and demanded Tingxian.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits came to the Qin River and demanded Tingxian.

sentences.zh: 竇莊東面河，道浚潛渡上流，繞賊後大噪，賊駭遁去。

translations.literal: Dou Village faced the river on the east; Daojun secretly crossed upstream, made a great clamor behind the bandits, and they fled in terror.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Village faced the river on the east. Daojun secretly crossed upstream, raised a great clamor behind the bandits, and they fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 未幾，官軍扼賊陵川，師潰，道浚據九仙臺以免。

translations.literal: Before long government troops blocked the bandits at Lingchuan; the army collapsed in rout, and Daojun held Jiuxian Terrace to escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Before long government troops blocked the bandits at Lingchuan. The army collapsed in rout, and Daojun held Jiuxian Terrace to escape harm.

sentences.zh: 十二月，廷憲知紫金梁、亂世王有隙，縱諜遣書間之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Tingxian knew Zijinliang and Luanshiwang were at odds and sent spies with letters to sow discord between them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Tingxian knew Zijinliang and Luanshiwang were at odds and sent spies with letters to sow discord between them.

sentences.zh: 亂世王果疑，遣其弟混世王就道浚乞降。

translations.literal: Luanshiwang indeed grew suspicious and sent his younger brother Hunshiwang to Daojun to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Luanshiwang indeed grew suspicious and sent his younger brother Hunshiwang to Daojun to beg surrender.

sentences.zh: 時統殷以失賊罷，許鼎臣來代，主進討。

translations.literal: At the time Tongyin was dismissed for losing the bandits; Xu Dingchen came to replace him and favored advancing to attack.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Tongyin was dismissed for losing the bandits. Xu Dingchen replaced him and favored advancing to attack.

sentences.zh: 道浚權詞難之曰：「斬紫金梁以來，乃得請。

translations.literal: Daojun used evasive words to make it difficult, saying: "Only when Zijinliang is beheaded may the request be granted.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun made evasive excuses, saying, "Only when Zijinliang is beheaded may the request be granted.

sentences.zh: 」混世王怏怏去，賊眾遂分部掠諸郡縣。

translations.literal: " Hunshiwang left discontented, and the bandit host then divided to plunder the various prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: " Hunshiwang left discontented, and the bandit host then divided to plunder the prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，官軍躡賊，自陽城而北。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year government troops pursued the bandits from Yangcheng northward.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year government troops pursued the bandits from Yangcheng northward.

sentences.zh: 道浚設伏三纏凹，擒賊渠滿天星等，巡撫鼎臣奏道浚功第一。

translations.literal: Daojun set an ambush at Sanchanao and captured bandit chiefs Mantianxing and others; Grand Coordinator Dingchen memorialized Daojun's merit as first.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun set an ambush at Sanchanao and captured bandit chiefs including Mantianxing. Grand Coordinator Dingchen memorialized Daojun's merit as first.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊陷沁水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the bandits took Qinshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the bandits took Qinshui.

sentences.zh: 沁水當賊沖，去來無時，道浚倡鄉人築堡五十四以守，賊五犯皆卻去，至是乃陷。

translations.literal: Qinshui lay on the bandits' route; they came and went without fixed times. Daojun urged the local people to build fifty-four fortresses to defend; the bandits attacked five times and were repelled each time—only now did it fall.
translations.idiomatic: Qinshui lay on the bandits' route, and they came and went without warning. Daojun urged the locals to build fifty-four fortresses for defense. The bandits attacked five times and were repelled each time—only now did the city fall.

sentences.zh: 道浚率家眾三百人馳赴擊賊，賊退徙十五里。

translations.literal: Daojun led three hundred of his household in haste to strike the bandits, and the bandits withdrew fifteen li.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun led three hundred of his household in haste to strike the bandits, and the bandits withdrew fifteen li.

sentences.zh: 道浚收散亡，捕賊眾，傾家囷以餉。

translations.literal: Daojun gathered the scattered and fugitive, captured bandit bands, and emptied the family granaries to supply provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun gathered the scattered and fugitive, captured bandit bands, and emptied the family granaries to supply provisions.

sentences.zh: 副使王肇生列狀上道浚功。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Wang Zhaosheng submitted a detailed report on Daojun's merit.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Wang Zhaosheng submitted a detailed report on Daojun's merit.

sentences.zh: 道浚故得罪清議，冀用軍功自湔祓，而言者劾其離伍冒功。

translations.literal: Daojun had formerly offended pure opinion and hoped to cleanse himself through military merit, but critics impeached him for leaving his post and claiming merit falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Daojun had formerly offended pure opinion and hoped to redeem himself through military merit, but critics impeached him for leaving his post and claiming merit falsely.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史馮明玠覆劾，謂沁城既失，不可言功，乃更戍海寧衛。

translations.literal: Touring censor Feng Mingjie impeached again, saying that since Qinshui city had fallen merit could not be claimed, and he was banished instead to the Haining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Feng Mingjie impeached again, saying that since Qinshui had fallen merit could not be claimed, and Daojun was banished instead to the Haining Guard.

sentences.zh: 何廷魁，字汝謙，山西威遠衛人。

translations.literal: He Tingkui, courtesy name Ruqian, was a native of the Weiyuan Guard in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He Tingkui, styled Ruqian, came from the Weiyuan Guard in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十九年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 29.

sentences.zh: 授涇縣知縣，調寧晉，遷刑部主事，歷歸德、衛輝、河南知府，西寧副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Jing County, transferred to Ningjin, promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, and served successively as prefect of Guide, Weihui, and Henan, and as vice commissioner of Xining.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Jing County, transferred to Ningjin, promoted to bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, and served as prefect of Guide, Weihui, and Henan, and as vice commissioner of Xining.

sentences.zh: 坐考功法，復為黎平知府。

translations.literal: He was demoted under the merit-evaluation law and again became prefect of Liping.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted under the merit-evaluation law and again became prefect of Liping.

sentences.zh: 會遼事棘，遷副使，分巡遼陽。

translations.literal: When Liaodong affairs grew critical he was transferred to vice commissioner and assigned to tour Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong affairs grew critical he was transferred to vice commissioner and assigned to tour Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 袁應泰納降，廷魁爭，不聽。

translations.literal: Yuan Yingtai accepted surrenders; Tingkui argued against it but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yingtai accepted surrenders. Tingkui argued against it but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 及瀋陽破，同事者遣孥歸，廷魁曰：「吾不敢為民望。

translations.literal: When Shenyang fell, colleagues sent wives and children home. Tingkui said: "I dare not set an example for the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenyang fell, colleagues sent wives and children home. Tingkui said, "I dare not set an example for the people.

sentences.zh: 」大清兵渡濠，廷魁請乘半濟急擊之。

translations.literal: " When the Great Qing army crossed the moat, Tingkui requested to strike them urgently while half across.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Qing army crossed the moat, Tingkui asked to strike them while half across.

sentences.zh: 俄薄城，圍未合，又請盡銳出禦。

translations.literal: Soon they pressed the city; the siege was not yet closed, and he again requested to lead all elite troops out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they pressed the city. The siege was not yet closed, and he again asked to lead all elite troops out to resist.

sentences.zh: 應泰並不從。

translations.literal: Yingtai would not agree to any of it.
translations.idiomatic: Yingtai would not agree to any of it.

sentences.zh: 遼陽破，廷魁懷印率其妾高氏、金氏投井死，婢仆從死者六人。

translations.literal: When Liaoyang fell, Tingkui clasped his seal and led his concubines Lady Gao and Lady Jin into a well to die; six maids and servants followed in death.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaoyang fell, Tingkui clasped his seal and led his concubines Lady Gao and Lady Jin into a well to die. Six maids and servants followed them in death.

sentences.zh: 都司徐國全聞之，亦自經公署。

translations.literal: Regional commander Xu Guoquan heard of it and also hanged himself in the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Xu Guoquan heard of it and also hanged himself in the government offices.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈光祿卿，再贈大理卿，賜祭葬，謚忠湣，世蔭錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was posthumously ennobled as Vice Minister of the Imperial Household, then posthumously ennobled again as Minister of Justice, granted sacrificial rites and burial, given the posthumous title Zhongmin, and his heirs granted hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Household and then Minister of Justice, granted state sacrifices and burial, given the posthumous title Zhongmin, and his heirs granted hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 國全贈恤如制。

translations.literal: Guoquan was granted posthumous consolation according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Guoquan received posthumous condolence grants according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 高邦佐，字以道，襄陵人。

translations.literal: Gao Bangzuo, courtesy name Yidao, was a native of Xiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Bangzuo, styled Yidao, came from Xiangling.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 23.

sentences.zh: 授壽光知縣，教民墾荒，招集流亡三千家。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Shouguang, taught the people to open wasteland, and gathered three thousand households of refugees.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Shouguang, taught the people to open wasteland, and gathered three thousand refugee households.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部主事、員外郎。

translations.literal: He served successively as bureau director and vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served as bureau director and vice director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 遷永平知府，浚濼河，築長堤。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Yongping, dredged the Luo River, and built a long dike.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Yongping, dredged the Luo River, and built a long dike.

sentences.zh: 裁抑稅使高淮，不敢大橫。

translations.literal: He restrained the tax commissioner Gao Huai, who did not dare act greatly overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: He restrained the tax commissioner Gao Huai, who did not dare act greatly overbearing.

sentences.zh: 遷天津兵備副使，平巨盜董時耀。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner for military preparations at Tianjin and pacified the great bandit Dong Shiyao.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice commissioner for military preparations at Tianjin and pacified the great bandit Dong Shiyao.

sentences.zh: 轉神木參政，屢破套寇沙計。

translations.literal: He moved to administrator of Shenmu and repeatedly defeated the Tao bandit Shaji.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to administrator of Shenmu and repeatedly defeated the Tao bandit Shaji.

sentences.zh: 以嫡母憂歸，補薊州道，坐調兵忤主者意，被劾歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on account of mourning for his legal mother, was reassigned to the Jizhou circuit, and was impeached and sent home for mobilizing troops against his superior's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to mourn his legal mother, was reassigned to the Jizhou circuit, and was impeached and sent home for mobilizing troops against his superior's wishes.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，遼陽破，起參政，分守廣寧。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, when Liaoyang fell, he was recalled as administrator and assigned to defend Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1, when Liaoyang fell, he was recalled as administrator and assigned to defend Guangning.

sentences.zh: 以母年八十餘，涕泣不忍去，母責以大義乃行。

translations.literal: Because his mother was more than eighty years old, he wept and could not bear to leave; his mother rebuked him with the greater duty and only then did he go.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was more than eighty. He wept and could not bear to leave until she rebuked him with the greater duty and he went.

sentences.zh: 熊廷弼、王化貞構隙，邦佐知遼事必敗，累乞歸。

translations.literal: Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen were at odds; Bangzuo knew Liaodong affairs must fail and repeatedly begged to return.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen were at odds. Bangzuo knew Liaodong affairs must fail and repeatedly begged to return.

sentences.zh: 方報允，而化貞棄廣寧逃。

translations.literal: Just as permission was reported granted, Huazhen abandoned Guangning and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Just as permission was reported granted, Huazhen abandoned Guangning and fled.

sentences.zh: 眾謂邦佐既請告，可入關。

translations.literal: The crowd said Bangzuo had already requested leave and could enter the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd said Bangzuo had already requested leave and could enter the passes.

sentences.zh: 邦佐叱曰：「吾一日未去，則一日封疆臣也，將安之！

translations.literal: Bangzuo rebuked them: "For one day I have not left, I am one day a frontier minister—where would I go!
translations.idiomatic: Bangzuo rebuked them: "For as long as I have not left, I am a frontier minister—where would I go!

sentences.zh: 」夜作書訣母，策騎趨右屯謁廷弼，言：「城中雖亂，敵尚未知。

translations.literal: " That night he wrote a farewell to his mother, spurred his horse to Youdun to visit Tingbi, and said: "Though the city is in disorder, the enemy does not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: " That night he wrote a farewell to his mother, spurred his horse to Youdun to visit Tingbi, and said, "Though the city is in disorder, the enemy does not yet know.

sentences.zh: 亟提兵入城，斬一二人，人心自定。

translations.literal: Hasten to lead troops into the city, behead one or two men, and popular sentiment will settle of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Hasten to lead troops into the city, behead one or two men, and the people will settle of themselves.

sentences.zh: 公即不行，請授邦佐兵赴難。

translations.literal: If you yourself will not go, grant Bangzuo troops to go to the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: If you yourself will not go, grant me troops to go to the crisis.

sentences.zh: 」廷弼不納，偕化貞並走。

translations.literal: " Tingbi would not accept and fled together with Huazhen.
translations.idiomatic: " Tingbi would not accept and fled together with Huazhen.

sentences.zh: 邦佐仰天長嘆，泣語從者曰：「經、撫俱逃，事去矣。

translations.literal: Bangzuo sighed long toward heaven and said weeping to his followers: "The supreme commander and grand coordinator have both fled—the affair is lost.
translations.idiomatic: Bangzuo sighed toward heaven and said weeping to his followers, "The supreme commander and grand coordinator have both fled—the affair is lost.

sentences.zh: 松山吾守地，當死此。

translations.literal: Songshan is the place I defend—I should die here.
translations.idiomatic: Songshan is the place I defend. I should die here.

sentences.zh: 汝歸報太夫人。

translations.literal: You return and report to the Lady Mother.
translations.idiomatic: You return and report to my mother.

sentences.zh: 」遂西向拜闕，復拜母，解印緩自經官舍。

translations.literal: " He then bowed west toward the palace, bowed again to his mother, removed his seal cord, and hanged himself in the government offices.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed west toward the palace, bowed again toward his mother, removed his seal cord, and hanged himself in the government offices.

sentences.zh: 仆高永曰：「主死，安可無從者。

translations.literal: His servant Gao Yong said: "When the master dies, how can there be none to follow?
translations.idiomatic: His servant Gao Yong said, "When the master dies, how can there be none to follow?

sentences.zh: 」亦自經於側。

translations.literal: " He too hanged himself at the side.
translations.idiomatic: " He too hanged himself beside him.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜祭葬，贈光祿卿，再贈太僕卿，謚忠節，世蔭錦衣百戶。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was granted sacrificial rites and burial, posthumously ennobled as Vice Minister of the Imperial Household, then posthumously ennobled again as Minister of the Imperial Stud, given the posthumous title Zhongjie, and his heirs granted hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was granted state sacrifices and burial, posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Household and then Minister of the Imperial Stud, given the posthumous title Zhongjie, and his heirs granted hereditary enrollment in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 邦佐與張銓、何廷魁皆山西人，詔建祠宣武門外，顏曰三忠。

translations.literal: Bangzuo, Zhang Quan, and He Tingkui were all Shanxi men; an edict ordered a shrine built outside Xuanwu Gate, inscribed "Three Loyal Ones."
translations.idiomatic: Bangzuo, Zhang Quan, and He Tingkui were all from Shanxi. An edict ordered a shrine built outside Xuanwu Gate, inscribed "Three Loyal Ones."

sentences.zh: 同時顧頤，以右參政分守遼海道。

translations.literal: At the same time Gu Yi, as right administrator, was assigned to defend the Liaohai circuit.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Gu Yi, as right administrator, was assigned to defend the Liaohai circuit.

sentences.zh: 廣寧之變，力屈自經。

translations.literal: At the Guangning disaster, his strength exhausted, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: At the Guangning disaster, his strength exhausted, he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 贈太僕少卿，世蔭本衛副千戶。

translations.literal: He was posthumously ennobled as Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, and his heirs granted hereditary vice battalion chief in his original guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, and his heirs granted hereditary vice battalion chief in his original guard.

sentences.zh: 崔儒秀，字儆初，陜州人。

translations.literal: Cui Ruxiu, courtesy name Jingchu, was a native of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Ruxiu, styled Jingchu, came from Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 26.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部郎中，遷開原兵備僉事。

translations.literal: He served successively as bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and was transferred to assistant commissioner for military preparations at Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue and was transferred to assistant commissioner for military preparations at Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時開原已失，儒秀募壯士，攜家辭墓行。

translations.literal: At that time Kaiyuan had already fallen; Ruxiu recruited brave men, took his family, bade farewell at the ancestral tombs, and set out.
translations.idiomatic: By then Kaiyuan had already fallen. Ruxiu recruited stalwart volunteers, gathered his family, paid his respects at the ancestral graves, and set out.

sentences.zh: 經略袁應泰以兵馬甲仗不足恃為憂，儒秀曰：「恃人有必死之心耳。

translations.literal: The frontier commissioner Yuan Yingtai worried that troops, horses, armor, and weapons could not be relied upon; Ruxiu said: "One relies on men having hearts resolved to die."
translations.idiomatic: Frontier Commissioner Yuan Yingtai worried that arms and armor alone could not be counted on. Ruxiu said, "What one can count on is men with the will to die."

sentences.zh: 」應泰深然之。

translations.literal: Yingtai deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Yingtai agreed wholeheartedly.

sentences.zh: 遼陽被圍，分守東城，矢集如雨，不少卻。

translations.literal: When Liaoyang was besieged, he was assigned to defend the east wall; arrows fell like rain, yet he did not retreat in the least.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaoyang came under siege, he was assigned to hold the eastern wall. Arrows fell like rain, yet he never gave ground.

sentences.zh: 會兵潰，儒秀痛哭，戎服北向拜，自經。

translations.literal: When the troops suddenly collapsed, Ruxiu wept bitterly, put on military dress, bowed northward, and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the army suddenly broke, Ruxiu wept bitterly, donned his uniform, bowed toward the north, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜恤視何廷魁，賜祠曰湣忠，以陳輔堯、段展配祀。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, he was granted posthumous relief equal to He Tingkui's, a shrine named Minzhong was bestowed, and Chen Fuyao and Duan Zhan were enshrined alongside him.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he received the same posthumous honors as He Tingkui. A shrine named "Lamented Loyalty" was granted, with Chen Fuyao and Duan Zhan enshrined alongside him.

sentences.zh: 輔堯，揚州人。

translations.literal: Fuyao was a native of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyao was from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 歷永平同知，轉餉出關，與自在知州段展駐瀋陽。

translations.literal: He served successively as vice magistrate of Yongping; while forwarding rations beyond the pass, he and Duan Zhan, magistrate of Zizai, were stationed at Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice magistrate of Yongping and, while transporting rations beyond the pass, was posted to Shenyang together with Duan Zhan, the magistrate of Zizai.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，日暈異常。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, the solar halo was unusually strange.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1, an unusual solar halo appeared.

sentences.zh: 展牒應泰言天象示警，宜豫防。

translations.literal: Zhan wrote a dispatch to Yingtai saying that the heavens showed warning signs and precaution should be taken in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan sent a memorial to Yingtai warning that heaven was sending omens and urging preventive measures.

sentences.zh: 逾月，瀋陽破，展死之。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Shenyang fell, and Zhan died defending it.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Shenyang fell, and Zhan died in its defense.

sentences.zh: 輔堯方奉命印烙，左右以無守土責，勸之去。

translations.literal: Fuyao was then carrying out orders to brand and seal livestock; those around him, noting he bore no obligation to defend the territory, urged him to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyao was then on duty branding livestock for the army. His companions, noting that he had no official duty to defend the city, urged him to flee.

sentences.zh: 輔堯曰：「孰非封疆臣，何去為。

translations.literal: Fuyao said: "Who is not a minister of the frontier realm—why should one leave?"
translations.idiomatic: Fuyao said, "Who among us is not a guardian of the realm's borders? Why should I leave?"

sentences.zh: 」望闕拜，拔刀自剄，與展並贈按察僉事。

translations.literal: He bowed toward the palace gate, drew his knife and cut his own throat; he and Zhan were both posthumously ennobled as assistant censorial commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed toward the palace, drew his knife, and cut his own throat. He and Zhan were both posthumously made assistant censorial commissioners.

sentences.zh: 輔堯官膠州時，有饋山繭者，受而懸之公幣中。

translations.literal: When Fuyao was magistrate of Jiaozhou, someone presented him mountain cocoons; he accepted them and hung them in the public hall.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Jiaozhou, Fuyao received a gift of mountain silk cocoons and hung them in the public hall for all to see.

sentences.zh: 展，涇陽舉人。

translations.literal: Zhan was a juren graduate from Jingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was a provincial graduate from Jingyang.

sentences.zh: 鄭國昌，邠州人。

translations.literal: Zheng Guochang was a native of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guochang came from Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Wanli he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He earned his jinshi degree in Wanli 35.

sentences.zh: 歷山西參政。

translations.literal: He served successively as Shanxi administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administrator in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年以按察使治兵永平，遷山西右布政使，上官奏留之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he served as provincial surveillance commissioner overseeing troops at Yongping; he was transferred to be right provincial administrative commissioner of Shanxi, but his superior memorialized to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he was made provincial surveillance commissioner at Yongping to oversee military affairs. Although promoted to right administrative commissioner of Shanxi, his superior petitioned to keep him in place.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，大清兵自京師東行，先使人伏文廟承塵上，主者不覺也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, Qing troops marched east from the capital; they first sent men to lie hidden above the ceiling beams in the Confucian temple, and the temple custodian did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 3, Qing forces marched east from Beijing. They first placed men in hiding above the ceiling of the Confucian temple, and the custodian noticed nothing.

sentences.zh: 初四日黎明登城，有守將左右之，國昌覺其異，捶之至死。

translations.literal: At dawn on the fourth day he ascended the wall; a defending general flanked him; Guochang sensed something amiss and beat him to death.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on the fourth, as he mounted the wall with a defending general beside him, Guochang sensed something was wrong and beat the man to death.

sentences.zh: 須臾，北樓火發，城遂破。

translations.literal: In a moment fire broke out at the northern tower, and the city was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later fire erupted at the northern tower, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 國昌自縊城上，中軍守備程應琦從之。

translations.literal: Guochang hanged himself atop the wall; the battalion garrison commander Cheng Yingqi followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang hanged himself on the wall. Battalion garrison commander Cheng Yingqi did likewise.

sentences.zh: 應琦妻奔告國昌妻，與之偕死。

translations.literal: Cheng Yingqi's wife ran to tell Guochang's wife, and the two died together.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Yingqi's wife ran to Guochang's wife, and the two women died together.

sentences.zh: 知府張鳳奇，推官盧成功，盧龍教諭趙允殖，副總兵焦延慶，東勝衛指揮張國翰及裏居中書舍人廖汝欽，武舉唐之俊，諸生韓洞原、周祚新、馮維京、胡起鳴、胡光奎、田種玉等十數人皆死。

translations.literal: Prefect Zhang Fengqi, assistant prefect Lu Chenggong, Lulong instructor Zhao Yunzhi, vice commander Jiao Yanqing, Dongsheng Guard commander Zhang Guohan, and along with the middle attendant at the palace secretariat Liao Ruqin, military licentiate Tang Zhijun, and students Han Dongyuan, Zhou Zuoxin, Feng Weijing, Hu Qiming, Hu Guangkui, Tian Chongyu, and more than ten others all died.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Fengqi, Assistant Prefect Lu Chenggong, Lulong Instructor Zhao Yunzhi, Vice Commander Jiao Yanqing, Dongsheng Guard Commander Zhang Guohan, palace secretariat attendant Liao Ruqin, military licentiate Tang Zhijun, and students Han Dongyuan, Zhou Zuoxin, Feng Weijing, Hu Qiming, Hu Guangkui, Tian Chongyu, and more than a dozen others all perished.

sentences.zh: 國昌、鳳奇一門盡死。

translations.literal: Guochang's and Fengqi's entire households died.
translations.idiomatic: Guochang and Fengqi lost their entire families in the catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈國昌太常卿，鳳奇光祿卿，並賜祭葬，蔭一子。

translations.literal: When reported, Guochang was posthumously ennobled as Minister of Ceremonies, Fengqi as Minister of the Imperial Household; both were granted sacrificial rites and burial, and one son was granted hereditary enrollment privilege.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, Guochang was posthumously made Minister of Ceremonies and Fengqi Minister of the Imperial Household. Both received state sacrifices and burial, and one son from each family received hereditary enrollment privileges.

sentences.zh: 成功等贈恤有差。

translations.literal: Chenggong and the others received varied posthumous relief.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong and the others received graded posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 鳳奇，陽曲人，起家鄉舉。

translations.literal: Fengqi was a native of Yangqu who began his career through the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Fengqi was from Yangqu and had entered service through the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 党還醇，字子貞，三原人。

translations.literal: Dang Huanchun, courtesy name Zizhen, was a native of Sanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dang Huanchun, styled Zizhen, came from Sanyuan.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Tianqi 5.

sentences.zh: 授休寧知縣，有善政，以父憂歸。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xiuning, governed well, and returned home upon his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Xiuning, he earned a reputation for good governance before returning home to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年服闋，起官良鄉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, when mourning ended, he was recalled to serve at Liangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended in Chongzhen 2, he was recalled to serve as magistrate of Liangxiang.

sentences.zh: 十二月，大清兵薄城，督吏民乘城拒守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Qing troops pressed the city; he supervised officials and people in mounting the walls to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Qing forces reached the city walls. Huanchun rallied officials and civilians to man the defenses.

sentences.zh: 或言縣小無兵，盍避去。

translations.literal: Some said the county was small and without troops—why not flee?
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that the county was small and had no troops; he ought to flee.

sentences.zh: 還醇毅然曰：「吾守土吏也，去將安之！

translations.literal: Huanchun declared resolutely: "I am an official charged with defending this land—if I leave, where shall I go!"
translations.idiomatic: Huanchun replied firmly, "I am the guardian of this district. If I flee, where shall I go?"

sentences.zh: 」救兵不至，力屈城破，與教諭安上達、訓導李廷表、典史史之棟、驛丞楊其禮並死焉。

translations.literal: Relief troops did not arrive; strength exhausted, the city fell; he died together with instructor An Shangda, trainer Li Tingbiao, clerk of records Shi Zhidong, and post station chief Yang Qili.
translations.idiomatic: Relief never came. When the defense collapsed and the city fell, he died together with Instructor An Shangda, Trainer Li Tingbiao, Records Clerk Shi Zhidong, and Post Station Chief Yang Qili.

sentences.zh: 事定，父老覓還醇屍，得之草間，赤身面縛，體被數槍，群哭而殮之。

translations.literal: When matters settled, elders searched for Huanchun's corpse, found it among the grass, naked and bound facing forward, the body pierced by several spears; the crowd wept and prepared it for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After the fighting ended, local elders found Huanchun's body in the grass—stripped naked, bound, and pierced by several spears. They wept as they prepared him for burial.

sentences.zh: 上達，貴州安順人。

translations.literal: Shangda was a native of Anshun in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shangda was from Anshun in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆末年舉於鄉，謁選得教諭，至日闔門死難。

translations.literal: In the late Wanli years he passed the provincial examination; upon reporting for appointment he received the post of instructor, and on the day he arrived the whole household died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial exam in the late Wanli period and received an instructor's appointment. On his very first day at Liangxiang, his entire household died in the disaster.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈還醇光祿丞，予祭葬，有司建祠，官其一子。

translations.literal: When reported, Huanchun was posthumously made Vice Director of the Imperial Household, granted sacrificial rites and burial; officials built a shrine, and one son received an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously made Huanchun Vice Director of the Imperial Household, granted him state sacrifices and burial, ordered a shrine built, and appointed one of his sons to office.

sentences.zh: 之棟等亦贈恤，給驛歸其喪。

translations.literal: Zhidong and the others also received posthumous relief, and courier service was provided to return their coffins.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidong and the others also received posthumous honors, and couriers were dispatched to return their remains home.

sentences.zh: 已而吏科上言：「還醇城亡與亡，之死靡貳，猶曰有守土責也。

translations.literal: Soon after the office of scrutiny memorialized: "Huanchun perished when the city fell and never wavered unto death—for one charged with defending the land that may be said as expected."
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Office of Scrutiny memorialized: "Huanchun died when the city fell and never wavered in his loyalty—a duty expected of one charged with defending the land."

sentences.zh: 上達、之棟等，微員末秩，亦能致命遂誌，有死無隕。

translations.literal: Shangda, Zhidong, and the others, low-ranking petty officials, could also give their lives to fulfill their purpose—dying without disgrace.
translations.idiomatic: Shangda, Zhidong, and the others were low-ranking officials, yet they too gave their lives without faltering, dying without disgrace.

sentences.zh: 宜破格褒崇，以為世勸。

translations.literal: They should receive exceptional commendation as encouragement to the world.
translations.idiomatic: They deserve exceptional honors to serve as an example for future generations.

sentences.zh: 朝廷必不惜今日之虛名，作將來之忠義，乃僅贈國學教職、良鄉主簿，於聖主憂恤之典謂何！

translations.literal: The court surely need not stint today's empty titles to foster tomorrow's loyalty—yet they were granted only National University instructor and Liangxiang registrar posthumous titles—what of the sage ruler's compassionate concern!
translations.idiomatic: Surely the court would not begrudge empty posthumous titles today to inspire loyalty tomorrow—yet these men received only the ranks of National University instructor and Liangxiang registrar. What does this say of our wise ruler's compassion for the loyal dead!

sentences.zh: 」帝感其言，下部更議，乃贈上達、廷表《五經》博士，與之棟等及千戶蕭如龍、何秉忠，百戶李蔭並配祀還醇祠。

translations.literal: The emperor was moved by these words and ordered further deliberation; then Shangda and Tingbiao were posthumously made Erudites of the Five Classics, and Zhidong and the others along with battalion chiefs Xiao Rulong and He Bingzhong, and company chief Li Yin, were all enshrined alongside Huanchun.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was moved and ordered a review. Shangda and Tingbiao were posthumously made Erudites of the Five Classics. Zhidong, battalion chiefs Xiao Rulong and He Bingzhong, company chief Li Yin, and others were all enshrined in Huanchun's shrine.

sentences.zh: 武舉陳蠡測、諸生梅友松等十五人，烈婦朱氏等十七人，並建坊旌表。

translations.literal: Military licentiate Chen Lice, students Mei Yousong and others—fifteen persons in all—and chaste women including Lady Zhu and others—seventeen in all—all had commemorative arches built in their honor.
translations.idiomatic: Commemorative arches were erected for military licentiate Chen Lice, students Mei Yousong and thirteen others, and seventeen chaste women including Lady Zhu.

sentences.zh: 順天府尹劉宗周以上達得死難之正，請贈翰苑宮坊，不報。

translations.literal: Liu Zongzhou, prefectural governor of Shuntian, because Shangda had died properly in calamity, requested posthumous honorary palace academy titles; no response was received.
translations.idiomatic: Shuntian Prefect Liu Zongzhou, citing Shangda's exemplary death, petitioned for posthumous palace academy titles. The request went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 是時，列城以死事聞者，更有香河知縣任光裕、濼州知州楊燫。

translations.literal: At that time among cities reporting death in service, there were also Xianghe magistrate Ren Guangyu and Luozhou prefect Yang Chi.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, other officials reported for dying in service included Xianghe Magistrate Ren Guangyu and Luozhou Prefect Yang Chi.

sentences.zh: 光裕贈恤如還醇，燫贈光祿少卿，並任一子。

translations.literal: Guangyu received posthumous relief like Huanchun; Chi was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Household; one son was granted office for each.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyu received the same posthumous honors as Huanchun. Chi was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Imperial Household. One son from each family received office.

sentences.zh: 李獻明，字思皇，壽光人。

translations.literal: Li Xianming, courtesy name Sihuang, was a native of Shouguang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianming, styled Sihuang, came from Shouguang.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年進士。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Chongzhen 1.

sentences.zh: 授保定推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed as reviewing officer at Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: He received an appointment as reviewing officer at Baoding.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月，大清兵臨遵化，巡撫王元雅與推官何天球、遵化知縣徐澤及先任知縣武起潛等憑城拒守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the following year Qing troops reached Zunhua; Grand Coordinator Wang Yuanya, reviewing officer He Tianqiu, Zunhua magistrate Xu Ze, and former magistrate Wu Qiqian and others defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the following year Qing forces reached Zunhua. Grand Coordinator Wang Yuanya, Reviewing Officer He Tianqiu, Zunhua Magistrate Xu Ze, former Magistrate Wu Qiqian, and others held the city walls.

sentences.zh: 時獻明以察核官庫駐城中。

translations.literal: At the time Xianming was stationed in the city to inspect the government treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Xianming happened to be in the city on an assignment to audit the government treasury.

sentences.zh: 或謂此邑非君所轄，去無罪。

translations.literal: Some said this county was not under his jurisdiction and that he would be blameless if he left.
translations.idiomatic: Some told him this county was not his jurisdiction and that he would bear no blame if he left.

sentences.zh: 獻明正色曰：「莫非王土，安敢見危避難。

translations.literal: Xianming said sternly: "Is it not all the king's land—how dare one flee when danger appears?"
translations.idiomatic: Xianming replied sternly, "Is this not the sovereign's land? How dare I flee when danger comes?"

sentences.zh: 」請守東門，城破死之。

translations.literal: He asked to defend the east gate and died when the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered to hold the east gate and died when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 元雅，太原人。

translations.literal: Yuanya was a native of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanya was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 為巡撫數月即遇變，自縊死。

translations.literal: Having served as grand coordinator only a few months, he met with disaster and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as grand coordinator only a few months when disaster struck; he hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 天球以永平推官理遵化軍餉。

translations.literal: Tianqiu, as reviewing officer of Yongping, managed Zunhua military rations.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqiu, the Yongping reviewing officer, was managing Zunhua's military rations.

sentences.zh: 澤，字兌若，襄陽人，獻明同年進士。

translations.literal: Ze, courtesy name Duiruo, was a native of Xiangyang and a jinshi graduate of the same year as Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: Ze, styled Duiruo, was from Xiangyang and had passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Xianming.

sentences.zh: 蒞任七日，與天球、起潛並殉難。

translations.literal: Having taken office for seven days, he died together with Tianqiu and Qiqian.
translations.idiomatic: He had been in office only seven days when he died alongside Tianqiu and Qiqian.

sentences.zh: 起潛，字用潛，進賢人。

translations.literal: Qiqian, courtesy name Yongqian, was a native of Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqian, styled Yongqian, came from Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Tianqi 5.

sentences.zh: 初為武清知縣，有諸生為人所訐，納金酒甕以獻。

translations.literal: At first he was magistrate of Wuqing; a student had been denounced by someone and presented gold in a wine jar as a bribe.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his career as magistrate of Wuqing, a student facing accusation tried to bribe him with gold hidden in a wine jar.

sentences.zh: 起潛召學官及諸生貧者數人，置甕庭中，謂之曰：「美酒不可獨享，與諸生共之。

translations.literal: Qiqian summoned the school officials and several poor students, placed the jar in the courtyard, and said to them: "Fine wine must not be enjoyed alone—let us share it with the students."
translations.idiomatic: Qiqian summoned the school officials and several impoverished students, set the jar in the courtyard, and said, "Good wine should not be enjoyed alone—let us share it with the students."

sentences.zh: 」酒盡，金見，其人惶恐請罪，即以金分畀貧者。

translations.literal: When the wine was finished the gold appeared; the man fearfully begged forgiveness, and Qiqian immediately divided the gold and gave it to the poor.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was gone the gold was revealed. The student pleaded for mercy in terror, and Qiqian divided the gold among the poor students.

sentences.zh: 治縣一年，有聲，調繁遵化。

translations.literal: After governing the county for one year with a good reputation, he was transferred to the demanding post at Zunhua.
translations.idiomatic: After a year of well-regarded service, he was transferred to the demanding post at Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 坐事被劾，解官候代，遂及於難。

translations.literal: He was impeached for an offense, relieved of office pending replacement, and thus met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached for an offense, he had been relieved pending replacement when disaster struck.

sentences.zh: 巡撫方大任論畿輔諸臣功罪，因言元雅有失城罪，而一死節概凜然，足以蓋愆。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Fang Daren assessed the merits and faults of officials in the capital region, saying that although Yuanya bore guilt for losing the city, his death in steadfast loyalty was imposing enough to cover his fault.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Fang Daren reviewed the merits and faults of officials in the capital region, noting that although Yuanya was guilty of losing the city, his resolute death in loyalty was enough to redeem the fault.

sentences.zh: 樞輔孫承宗請恤殉難諸臣，亦首元雅。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong requested relief for officials who died in calamity, also listing Yuanya first.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong petitioned for honors for those who died in the disaster, placing Yuanya first on the list.

sentences.zh: 帝贈獻明、天球光祿少卿，澤光祿丞，俱蔭一子。

translations.literal: The emperor posthumously made Xianming and Tianqiu Vice Ministers of the Imperial Household, Ze Vice Director of the Imperial Household, and granted each one son hereditary enrollment privilege.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posthumously made Xianming and Tianqiu Vice Ministers of the Imperial Household and Ze Vice Director of the Imperial Household. One son from each family received hereditary enrollment privileges.

sentences.zh: 元雅以大吏失城，贈恤不及。

translations.literal: Because Yuanya was a high official who lost a city, posthumous relief did not reach him.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior official who had lost a city, Yuanya received no posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 張春，字泰宇，同州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Chun, courtesy name Taiyu, was a native of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chun, styled Taiyu, came from Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十八年舉於鄉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Wanli he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in Wanli 28.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部主事，勵操行，善談兵。

translations.literal: He served successively as bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, cultivated his conduct, and was skilled at discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He served as bureau director in the Ministry of Justice, was known for his integrity, and had a gift for military strategy.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，遼東西盡失，廷議急邊才，擢山東僉事，永平、燕建二路兵備道。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi, when east and west Liaodong were entirely lost, the court debated urgently for frontier talent; he was promoted to Shandong assistant commissioner as military intendant of the Yongping and Yanjian circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 2, with Liaodong lost on both flanks, the court urgently sought frontier talent and promoted him to Shandong assistant commissioner as military intendant of the Yongping and Yanjian circuits.

sentences.zh: 時大軍屯山海關，永平為孔道，士馬絡繹，關外難民雲集。

translations.literal: At the time the main army was encamped at Shanhaiguan; Yongping was the vital corridor; troops and horses passed in unbroken streams, and refugees beyond the pass gathered like clouds.
translations.idiomatic: The main army was encamped at Shanhaiguan, and Yongping lay on the vital supply route. Troops and horses streamed through without pause, and refugees from beyond the pass gathered in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 春運籌有方，事就理而民不病。

translations.literal: Chun planned with method; affairs were brought to order and the people were not harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Chun managed affairs with skill, bringing order without burdening the people.

sentences.zh: 累轉副吏、參政，仍故官。

translations.literal: He was promoted successively to vice minister and administrator, while retaining his original duties.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to vice minister and administrator while continuing in his original post.

sentences.zh: 七年，哈刺慎部長汪燒餅者，擁眾窺桃林口，春督守將擒三人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Wang Shaobing, a chieftain of the Khalkha tribe, gathered a force to spy on Taolin Pass; Chun supervised the defending generals in capturing three men.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 7, Wang Shaobing, a Khalkha chieftain, gathered troops to probe Taolin Pass. Chun directed the garrison commanders to capture three of them.

sentences.zh: 燒餅叩關願受罰，春等責數之，誓不敢叛。

translations.literal: Shaobing came to the pass to beg punishment; Chun and the others rebuked him at length, and he swore never again to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Shaobing came to the pass to submit to punishment. Chun and his colleagues rebuked him sharply, and he swore never to rebel again.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，永平失守，起春永平兵備參議。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Yongping fell; Chun was recalled as Yongping military intendant and administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Chongzhen 3, after Yongping fell, Chun was recalled as Yongping military intendant and administrator.

sentences.zh: 春言：「永平統五縣一州，今郡城及灤州、遷安並失，昌黎、樂亭、撫寧又關內道所轄。

translations.literal: Chun said: "Yongping governs five counties and one prefecture; now the prefectural seat and Luanzhou and Qian'an have all fallen, while Changli, Leting, and Funing are under the jurisdiction of the interior circuit."
translations.idiomatic: Chun wrote: "Yongping governs five counties and one prefecture. The prefectural seat, Luanzhou, and Qian'an have all fallen, while Changli, Leting, and Funing lie under the interior circuit."

sentences.zh: 臣寄跡無所，當駐何城？

translations.literal: Your servant has nowhere to lodge—at which city should he be stationed?
translations.idiomatic: I have nowhere to establish my headquarters—which city should I hold?

sentences.zh: 臣以兵備名官，而實無一兵，操空拳入虎穴，安能濟事。

translations.literal: Your servant bears the title of military intendant yet in truth has not a single soldier; wielding empty fists into a tiger's den, how can affairs be accomplished?
translations.idiomatic: I hold the title of military intendant but command not a single soldier. Going into the tiger's den with empty hands, how can I accomplish anything?

sentences.zh: 乞於赴援大將中，敕一人與臣同事，臣亦招舊日義勇率之自效。

translations.literal: I beg that from among the great generals coming to the relief, one be ordered to work with your servant; your servant will also recruit former volunteers and lead them to serve.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that one of the relief generals be ordered to serve alongside me, and that I be allowed to recruit my former volunteers and lead them into action.

sentences.zh: 臣身已許此城，不敢少規避。

translations.literal: Your servant's person has already been pledged to this city and dares not shrink back in the least.
translations.idiomatic: I have already pledged my life to this city and will not shrink from the task.

sentences.zh: 但必求實濟封疆，此臣區區之忠，所以報聖明而盡臣職也。

translations.literal: But one must seek real benefit for the frontier realm—this is your servant's humble loyalty, by which to repay the sage clarity and fulfill his ministerial duty.
translations.idiomatic: But I must ask for the means to truly defend the frontier—that is the whole of my loyalty, and how I mean to repay the emperor and fulfill my duty.

sentences.zh: 」因言兵事不可預泄，乞賜陛見，面陳方略，帝許之。

translations.literal: He further said that military affairs must not be disclosed in advance, and begged an audience to present strategy in person; the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: He added that military plans could not be disclosed in writing and requested an audience to present his strategy in person. The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 既入對，帝數稱善，進春參政。

translations.literal: After he entered for audience, the emperor repeatedly praised him and promoted Chun to administrator.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience, the emperor repeatedly expressed approval and promoted Chun to administrator.

sentences.zh: 已而偕諸將收復永平諸城，論功加太僕少卿，仍蒞兵備事，候巡撫缺推用。

translations.literal: Soon after, together with the generals he recovered the cities of Yongping; for merit he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, still overseeing military preparations, awaiting recommendation when the grand coordinator post fell vacant.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the generals in recovering the Yongping cities. For his merit he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, continued to oversee military preparations, and was slated for the grand coordinator post when it opened.

sentences.zh: 時乙榜起家者多授節鉞，而春獨需後命，以無援於朝也。

translations.literal: At the time many who entered service through the second-rank examination were granted command seals, yet Chun alone had to await a later appointment, because he had no patron at court.
translations.idiomatic: Many provincial graduates were being given military commands, but Chun alone had to wait for a later appointment—he had no patron at court.

sentences.zh: 永平當兵燹之余，閭閻困敝，春盡心撫恤，人益懷之。

translations.literal: Yongping, in the aftermath of war and fire, had exhausted households; Chun devoted himself to relief and care, and the people came to esteem him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping lay in ruins after the fighting, its people exhausted. Chun devoted himself to relief and care, and the people grew ever more devoted to him.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，大清兵圍大淩河新城，命春監總兵吳襄、宋偉軍馳救。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year Qing troops besieged the new city at Dalinghe; Chun was ordered to supervise the armies of regional commanders Wu Xiang and Song Wei in a rapid relief march.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Chongzhen 4, Qing forces besieged the new city at Dalinghe. Chun was ordered to supervise regional commanders Wu Xiang and Song Wei in a rapid relief march.

sentences.zh: 九月二十四日渡小淩河。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month they crossed the Xiaoling River.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-fourth of the ninth month the relief force crossed the Xiaoling River.

sentences.zh: 越三日次長山，距城十五里，大清兵以二萬騎來逆戰。

translations.literal: Three days later they halted at Changshan, fifteen li from the city; the Great Qing force came with twenty thousand cavalry to meet them in battle.
