translations.literal: Liu Shijing, also of unknown origin, served as magistrate of Shuyang and had a reputation for forceful competence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shijing, likewise of unknown origin, was magistrate of Shuyang and was known as a resolute administrator.

sentences.zh: 竭力捍城，城破死之。

translations.literal: He exerted all his strength to defend the city and died when it fell.
translations.idiomatic: He fought with everything he had to hold the city and died when it was lost.

sentences.zh: 贈山東僉事。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Shandong Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Shandong vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 其時，城破殉難者，壽張王大年、曹州楚煙、滕縣劉弘緒數人。

translations.literal: At that time among those who died martyred when cities fell were Wang Danian of Shouzhang, Chu Yan of Caozhou, Liu Hongxu of Teng County, and several others.
translations.idiomatic: Others who died when their cities fell included Wang Danian of Shouzhang, Chu Yan of Caozhou, and Liu Hongxu of Teng County.

sentences.zh: 大年舉進士，歷御史，加太僕少卿，以附魏忠賢名持逆案，至是盡節死。

translations.literal: Danian passed the jinshi examination, served as censor, was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, was named in the factional reverse case for supporting Wei Zhongxian, and now died with full integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Danian had passed the jinshi, served as censor, and risen to vice minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud; he had been implicated in the purge of Wei Zhongxian's faction, but now died with honor intact.

sentences.zh: 煙舉進士，歷戶部主事，解職歸。

translations.literal: Yan passed the jinshi examination, served as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue, and resigned to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was a jinshi who had served as principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue before retiring home.

sentences.zh: 及城失守，力抗，子鳳苞以身翼之，皆被殺。

translations.literal: When the city was lost he resisted fiercely; his son Fengbao shielded him with his body, and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he fought on; his son Fengbao spread his body over him to protect him, and both were slain.

sentences.zh: 妻趙觸柱死。

translations.literal: His wife Zhao died by striking a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Zhao dashed herself against a pillar and died.

sentences.zh: 弘緒歷車駕郎中，遇變死。

translations.literal: Hongxu had served as a director in the Directorate of Imperial Transport and died when crisis struck.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxu had served in the Directorate of Imperial Transport and died in the upheaval.

sentences.zh: 鄧藩錫，字晉伯，金壇人。

translations.literal: Deng Fanshi, styled Jinbo, was a native of Jintan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Fanshi, styled Jinbo, came from Jintan.

sentences.zh: 崇禎七年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the seventh year of Chongzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in Chongzhen 7.

sentences.zh: 歷南京兵部主事。

translations.literal: He served as a principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He served as principal secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 十五年遷袞州知府，甫抵任，已聞大清兵入塞，亟繕守具。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was transferred to be prefect of Yanzhou; he had barely reached his post when he heard the Great Qing army had entered the frontier passes and urgently prepared defenses.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 15 he was appointed prefect of Yanzhou; scarcely had he arrived when word came that the Qing army had crossed the frontier, and he hurriedly readied the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 未幾，四萬騎薄城下，藩錫走告魯王曰：「郡有吏，國有王，猶同舟也。

translations.literal: Before long forty thousand horsemen pressed up to the city walls; Fanshi ran to tell the Prince of Lu: "The prefecture has its officials and the state has its prince — we are like passengers in the same boat."
translations.idiomatic: Soon forty thousand cavalry were at the walls; Fanshi rushed to the Prince of Lu and said, "A prefecture has its magistrates and a kingdom its prince — we are all in the same boat."

sentences.zh: 列城失守，皆由貴家惜金錢，而令窶人、餓夫列陴捍禦。

translations.literal: Cities fall one after another because the wealthy families begrudge their money while the poor and starving are made to line the battlements in defense.
translations.idiomatic: City after city falls because the rich cling to their gold while the poor and hungry are sent to man the walls.

sentences.zh: 夫城郭者，我之命也。

translations.literal: The city walls are our lives.
translations.idiomatic: The walls are our very lives.

sentences.zh: 財賄者，人之命也。

translations.literal: Wealth is the people's lives.
translations.idiomatic: Wealth is what keeps the people alive.

sentences.zh: 我不能畀彼以命，而望彼畀我以命乎？

translations.literal: If I will not give them what keeps them alive, how can I expect them to give me my life?
translations.idiomatic: How can I refuse them the means to live and still expect them to die for me?

sentences.zh: 王誠散積儲以鼓士氣，城猶可存。

translations.literal: If Your Highness will truly distribute stored provisions to raise morale, the city may yet be saved.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Highness will open the granaries and rouse the men's spirits, the city can still be held.

sentences.zh: 不然，大事一去，悔無及矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, once the great cause is lost, regret will come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, once the cause is lost, it will be too late for regret.

sentences.zh: 」王不能從。

translations.literal: " The prince could not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: " The prince would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 藩錫與監軍參議王維新，同知譚絲、曾文蔚，通判閻鼎，推官李昌期，滋陽知縣郝芳聲，副將丁文明，長史俞起蛟及裏居給事中範淑泰等分門死守。

translations.literal: Fanshi, together with supervising military affairs participant Wang Weixin, vice prefects Tan Si and Zeng Wenwei, subprefect Yan Ding, investigating magistrate Li Changqi, Ziyang Magistrate Hao Fangsheng, deputy general Ding Wenming, chief secretary Yu Qijiao, and retired supervising secretary Fan Shutai and others, held the gates and defended to the death.
translations.idiomatic: Fanshi, military supervisor Wang Weixin, vice prefects Tan Si and Zeng Wenwei, subprefect Yan Ding, investigating magistrate Li Changqi, Ziyang magistrate Hao Fangsheng, deputy general Ding Wenming, chief secretary Yu Qijiao, and the retired supervising secretary Fan Shutai divided the gates among themselves and held to the last.

sentences.zh: 至十二月八日，力不支，城破，維新猶力戰，被二十一創乃死。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the twelfth month their strength failed, the city fell, and Weixin still fought fiercely, receiving twenty-one wounds before he died.
translations.idiomatic: On the eighth day of the twelfth month the defense collapsed; even after the city fell Weixin kept fighting until twenty-one wounds brought him down.

sentences.zh: 藩錫受縛不降，被殺，其妾攜稚子投井死。

translations.literal: Fanshi was bound but would not submit and was killed; his concubine took their young child and threw herself into a well.
translations.idiomatic: Fanshi was captured but refused to yield and was executed; his concubine leapt into a well with their infant son.

sentences.zh: 魯王以派亦被殺。

translations.literal: The Prince of Lu, Yipai, was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Lu Yipai was killed as well.

sentences.zh: 昌期，永年人。

translations.literal: Changqi was a native of Yongnian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Changqi came from Yongnian.

sentences.zh: 芳聲，忻州人。

translations.literal: Hao Fangsheng was a native of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Fangsheng came from Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 並起家進士。

translations.literal: Both had begun their careers as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Both were jinshi by origin.

sentences.zh: 昌期嘗監軍破土寇萬，眾推其才。

translations.literal: Changqi had once supervised troops in breaking a bandit force of ten thousand, and the people praised his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Changqi had once directed troops against a ten-thousand-man bandit force, and his ability was widely admired.

sentences.zh: 芳聲治縣有聲。

translations.literal: Fang sheng had a reputation for governing his county well.
translations.idiomatic: Fang sheng was known for effective county administration.

sentences.zh: 至是皆死。

translations.literal: At this time both died.
translations.idiomatic: Both died in the defense.

sentences.zh: 起蛟，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Qijiao was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Qijiao came from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 由貢生歷官魯府左長史，相憲王。

translations.literal: Through tribute graduate selection he rose to Left Chief Secretary of the Lu princely establishment and served as adviser to the Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute graduate, he rose to left chief secretary of the Lu princely household and served as adviser to Prince Xian of Lu.

sentences.zh: 及惠王立，欲易世子，起蛟力諫乃已。

translations.literal: When Prince Hui succeeded to the title and wished to replace the heir, Qijiao remonstrated forcefully until he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Hui took the title and tried to displace the heir apparent, Qijiao argued him down until he gave up the plan.

sentences.zh: 世子嗣位，值歲凶，勸王振貸，自出粟二千石佐之。

translations.literal: When the heir succeeded, famine struck; he urged the prince to provide relief grain and himself contributed two thousand shi to assist.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir came to the title, a famine year followed; he urged the prince to open relief stores and himself gave two thousand shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 大盜李青山率眾來犯，偕淑泰出擊，大破其眾。

translations.literal: The great bandit Li Qingshan led his followers to attack; Qijiao went out with Shutai to strike them and routed their force.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit chieftain Li Qingshan marched against the city, Qijiao sallied forth with Shutai and smashed his army.

sentences.zh: 及王被難，起蛟率親屬二十三人殉之。

translations.literal: When the prince met disaster, Qijiao led twenty-three kinsmen to die with him.
translations.idiomatic: When disaster befell the prince, Qijiao led twenty-three members of his family to die at his side.

sentences.zh: 文明亦戰死。

translations.literal: Wenming also died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wenming also fell in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈維新光祿卿，藩錫太僕少卿，昌期僉事，余贈恤有差。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, Weixin was posthumously granted Grand Master for the Imperial Insignia, Fan Xi was granted Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, Changqi was granted Assistant Commissioner, and the rest were granted posthumous honors and pensions according to their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When word of their deaths reached the throne, Wang Weixin was posthumously made Grand Master for the Imperial Insignia, Deng Fanxi Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud, and Li Changqi an Assistant Commissioner; the others received posthumous honors and pensions in proportion to their rank.

sentences.zh: 有樊吉人者，元城人。

translations.literal: There was one Fan Jiren, a man of Yuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Fan Jiren, a native of Yuancheng.

sentences.zh: 由進士知滋陽，累擢山東兵備僉事。

translations.literal: Having entered through the jinshi degree, he served as magistrate of Ziyang; he was repeatedly promoted to Assistant Commissioner for Military Affairs in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi degree-holder, he served as magistrate of Ziyang and was steadily promoted to Assistant Commissioner for Military Affairs in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 未行遇變，自刎死。

translations.literal: Before he could take up his post, he encountered the upheaval and slit his own throat to die.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the new post, the crisis broke out, and he cut his own throat and died.

sentences.zh: 淑泰自有傳。

translations.literal: Shu Tai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Shutai has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 時又有天津參將賀秉鉞者，泰寧左衛人。

translations.literal: At the time there was also the Deputy Commander of Tianjin, He Bingyue, a man of Taiping Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was also He Bingyue, Deputy Commander of Tianjin, a native of Taiping Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 崇禎四年第武科一甲第三，亦以扶父柩至臨清，巷戰終日，矢盡，被執死。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of the Chongzhen reign he placed third in the first rank of the military examination; he likewise escorted his father's coffin to Linqing, fought in the streets all day, his arrows were exhausted, and he was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of the Chongzhen reign he placed third among the top tier of the military examinations. He too had been escorting his father's coffin to Linqing when he fought street by street all day; when his arrows ran out, he was taken and killed.
